english: God-born one, the herdsman of our tribe stole a cow. Why did he steal it? He stole it from his own brother. Let him give it back to him(?) and then let the two drink together. This I have told him.
uncertain: h₂éwih₁ unclear (to the grandfather? sheep dual?)
swṓd bʰréh₂tr̥s read as ablative 'from his own brother'
dh₃yéh₁t read as optative of deh₃- 'give'

english: Dear friend, tell me truly where you dwell. I dwell by the water. I and my wife [have] a field on the ploughland. And where do you dwell? I dwell in the village of the hills.

Mother, tell me: which man do I know who deceives? I watched his two guests. The one who deceives trembles before his guests. And why did you not tremble before his guests? Now, daughter, do not follow him.
uncertain: ǵn̥néh₃oh₂ — 1sg 'I know'? syntax of the first sentence unclear
tr̥mtés participle in a predicate position

english: O rich-in-horses, the tribe is hungry. Shall we kill the horses? Do not kill them. A tribe without horses perishes. Then what shall we eat? Eat acorns and cook the sheep.
Mother, why do I not succeed with the elders? Listen, and afterwards you will succeed. Do not lament. And why do they not listen to me? Now hold back your word. The word of a good man is heard.
Sister, I saw fire on the hill. Enemies are burning it; their war-band is coming. Shall we run to the men? Go quickly, and they come ... I will stand here with the dogs.
